note: OBSERVED as the spike's finding 4: before needle_reset was called between prompts, under-specified prompts reused values from earlier turns and the reasoning text said so outright. The prior turn is supplied here as COMPLETED history, not as a pending slot request. A completed action is not an open slot, and reaching into it for a value the user did not repeat is the failure.

The plausible-inference trap at its most expensive. "Them" probably does mean Marco, and probably is not evidence — the user may have just been called by somebody else, which is usually why they said it this way. Vesta resolves references; the router does not guess them.

priorTurns.utterance: Remind me to call the dentist at 3pm.

note: A second reminder at a new time, about something the user has not said yet. Carrying the earlier text forward produces a notification with the wrong content at the right time — which is harder to notice than a wrong time.
A correction REPLACES a known slot rather than adding one. The state block carries the value being corrected, so the router does not have to remember it.
One slot replaced, the other kept verbatim. Re-deriving the message body here would rewrite what the user already approved.

utterance: actually set a timer for 5 minutes instead
note: A pending action is not a funnel. "5 minutes" arriving while an alarm is pending must not become an alarm time — the user changed their mind about the tool, not just the value.

priorTurns.utterance: What do I have on Thursday?

note: The stale-context case on an OPTIONAL argument, which the missing-slot rule cannot cover. Carrying Thursday forward is not a refusable fabrication — it is a silently wrong answer about a different day.
